To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
biomimetic approach has been employed for the synthesis of hydroxyapatite nanoparticle with a size of 40 nm and a Ca/P ratio of 1·67, with the help of a biomolecule, namely bovine serum albumine.
biomimetic synthesis of hydroxyapatite in presence of bovine serum albumine (BSA) results in the formation of monodisperesized particles of 30–40nm size with narrow size distribution.
the biomimetic synthesis of nanoparticles with uniform size and shape is possible and the biomimetic nanoparticles can be used for biomedical applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of biomimetically derived nanoparticles with uniform size and shape, with controlled crystallinity and stoichiometry, which can be sintered to obtain dense and strong ceramic bodies.
the synthesis of monodispersed nanoparticles of hydroxyapatite using biomimetic approach and their sintering behavior.
the synthesis and characterization of biomimetically prepared hydroxyapatite (HAp) nanoparticles and its sintering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the protein concentration plays a crucial role in the synthesis of hydroxyapatite.
biomimetics is an excellent tool for synthesis of nanoparticles and the results of this study can be used as a reference to design nanoparticles for specific applications.
biomimetically synthesized nanoparticles are a viable alternative to the conventional chemical methods for synthesis of nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of biomimetic nanoparticles with controlled size and morphology has been demonstrated and the sintering behavior of the biomimetic hydroxapatite nanoparticles has been studied.
the biomimetically synthesized particles have been successfully sintered into dense compacts without any grain growth.

the biomimetic synthesis of hydroxyapatite using a biomolecule like bovine serum albumine is a promising route to obtain monodisperse, spherical nanoparticles with uniform morphology, size, shape and narrow size distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein mediated synthesis of nanoparticles can be used to tailor the properties of the particles for specific applications.
it is possible to control the particle size of hydroxyapatite synthesized by the biomimetic route and to achieve a degree of crystallinity that is suitable for biomedical applications.
biomimetic synthesis of nanoparticles is a promising route for the synthesis of biomaterials with desired properties.
